requirements.statement: The sole-owner account retention sweep computes lineage custody in bounded passes (at most CUSTODY_PASS_ROWS history rows per pass, rowid windows), releases an answer only when one cycle has seen every row, and that answer equals the exact custody restricted to lineage edge keys; a live run is never missed at any position or bound; a cycle the change watch invalidates is discarded (S14F-6).
A custody pass on a large (60k-run) history stays well inside the S7 owner request bound (LEDGER_REQUEST_WAIT_MS/8).
sweep_account_retention uses the paged scan and never the whole-history custody; open and the upgrade still compute custody whole (S14E-1/2 pin that query).

One cutoff per custody cycle, fixed at its start: a later clock judges against the earlier (more protective) cutoff, and a pass whose clock is before the cycle start restarts the cycle, so neither a clock rollback nor a forward jump lets a completed or pruning cycle hold less than the whole custody at that time.

Every owner pass bounds its total work (lineage edges read by key page, history rows, protected-path walk steps with one visited set, deletions) to CUSTODY_PASS_ROWS units; a long overlapping chain completes over many passes each within the bound and equals the whole-scan prune; the whole prune walks each edge once.

A cycle continues only while a per-connection TEMP change watch (any change that could add custody for an edge key, or any lineage insert/update), PRAGMA data_version and main.schema_version are unchanged on the same connection: a delete+reinsert behind the cursor restoring the max rowid is still found, a VACUUM or another connection's commit mid-cycle discards the cycle, and ledger maintenance VACUUM resets the owner scan.

Under fixed-seed random interleavings of inserts, releases, deletes, delete+reinsert, binding/hold changes, new edges, clock moves, VACUUM, other-connection commits and the commit-before-write-lock race between passes, every completed paged answer covers the whole answer and no pruning pass deletes an edge the whole computation protects at that moment; once quiet, the paged prune equals the whole prune.

A pruning pass rechecks the change watch, PRAGMA data_version and main.schema_version inside its write transaction (write lock held) before any delete; custody another connection commits after the pass-start checks abandons that prune and restarts the cycle (two real connections on one file, WAL and rollback journal).

The completion walk consumes the custody set a budget at a time (no copy of it) and a reset is O(1): the old cycle's containers are handed to a drop list emptied within later passes' budgets, so no pass exceeds CUSTODY_PASS_ROWS units at completion or reset with 2,000 keys.

Exclusive maintenance waits at most MAINTENANCE_READER_WAIT_S for health-copy readers; a stalled worker fails the attempt with a plain LedgerError, leaves the store unchanged and the reader registered, and a later attempt succeeds once the worker ends.
